prayerExcerpt.en-US: St. Stanislas teaches us in every trial of life, and above all in the hour of death, to have recourse to our patron Saint, and to trust without fear to his aid.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: São Estanislau ensina-nos, em toda provação da vida, e acima de tudo na hora da morte, a recorrer ao nosso Santo padroeiro, e a confiar sem temor em seu auxílio.

meta.face: A Polish youth of seventeen, BEARDLESS, with a fair, fresh complexion and a face BROAD across the EYES and cheekbones, narrowing gently to a small, ROUNDED chin — a smooth, rounded forehead, a LONG, STRAIGHT nose, BROAD at its base, LARGE, dark-brown eyes set WIDE under HEAVY, half-lowered upper lids, dark brows ARCHED HIGH above them, smooth, softly full cheeks, a SMALL, FULL, slightly POUTING mouth with a SHORT upper lip; dark-brown hair cut short and straight across the brow; the look bright and gentle, lifted a little. Not the round, short-nosed boy pancras, the upturned-nosed herman_joseph, the tousle-curled carlo_acutis, the flat-cheeked, low-bridged venantius_camerino, the long, narrow casimir, the triangular peter_luxemburg or the straw-fair, narrow-faced student of john_kanty.
meta.basis: The portrait on English Wikipedia (captioned only 'Scipione Delfine portrait'; its date was not established) shows a broad young face with large, heavy-lidded dark eyes, a long straight nose and a small full mouth, which the card follows; the cassock, the novitiate in Rome and his joy are from the book and the Martyrology.
